# Data Quality

## Definition

Data Quality is the degree to which data is fit for its intended uses, assessed against explicit requirements along defined [[Data Quality Dimension|quality dimensions]].

## Explanation

Quality is **relative to use**: the same data can be adequate for trend reporting and inadequate for invoicing. Therefore quality requirements must be explicit, owned and measurable. Architecture contributes by: placing controls near the source ([[Quality Is Managed at the Source]]), building [[Data Quality Gate|quality gates]] into flows, providing lineage for root-cause analysis, and designing models that prevent invalid states.

Relevant standards include [[ISO IEC 25012 Data Quality Model]] (a quality model for data) and [[ISO 8000 Data Quality]] (a series on data quality and master data exchange).

## Distinctions

- Data quality vs **data validation**: validation is one mechanism to check quality rules.
- Data quality vs **metadata quality**: metadata has quality too (completeness of definitions, accuracy of lineage).

## Examples

- "99.5% of active policies have a valid postal code" as a measurable requirement.
